Title: How to Write a Good GitHub Issue That Gets Answered
Desc: Learn how to write clear, structured, and actionable GitHub issues that improve your chances of getting fast responses from maintainers and contributors.
Author: MyWrite
Data:
## A bad GitHub issue usually looks like this:

```text
It doesn't work
```

And then nothing else.

Maintainers cannot help with that.

A good issue is clear, structured, and actionable.

It saves time for everyone.

---

## Why Good Issues Matter

Open source projects depend on communication.

A well-written issue:

- Gets faster responses
- Reduces confusion
- Helps maintainers reproduce bugs
- Improves chances of a fix

Think of it like this:

```text
Clear Issue
↓
Faster Fix
↓
Better Project
```

---

## Start With a Clear Title

Bad:

```text
Bug in login
```

Good:

```text
Login fails with 401 error after password reset
```

The title should explain the problem in one line.

---

## Describe the Problem Clearly

Explain what is happening.

Include:

- What you expected
- What actually happened
- When it started

Example:

```text
Expected: User should be logged in after submitting form
Actual: Page returns 401 error
```

---

## Provide Steps to Reproduce

This is one of the most important parts.

Example:

```text
1. Go to login page
2. Enter valid credentials
3. Click submit
4. See error 401
```

If maintainers can reproduce the issue, fixing it becomes much easier.

---

## Include Environment Details

Always add technical context:

- OS (Windows, macOS, Linux)
- Browser version
- Node.js version (if relevant)
- Package version

Example:

```text
OS: Windows 11
Browser: Chrome 120
Node: 20.x
```

---

## Add Screenshots or Logs

Visual evidence helps a lot.

Include:

- Screenshots
- Console errors
- Network logs
- Terminal output

Example:

```text
TypeError: Cannot read property 'data' of undefined
```

---

## Be Specific, Not Vague

Vague:

```text
App is broken
```

Specific:

```text
Dashboard fails to load after API returns 500 error on /api/users endpoint
```

Specific issues are easier to solve.

---

## Explain Impact

Help maintainers understand severity.

Example:

```text
This bug prevents users from completing checkout, affecting all paid transactions.
```

Impact helps prioritize issues.

---

## One Issue = One Problem

Avoid combining multiple issues.

Bad:

```text
Login broken + UI bug + API issue
```

Good:

```text
Login fails with 401 error after password reset
```

---

## Check Before Submitting

Before posting:

- Search existing issues
- Check documentation
- Verify it's not already reported

This avoids duplicates.

---

![Open source collaboration and issue tracking dashboard](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1516321318423-f06f85e504b3)

## Use Proper Labels (If Available)

Some repositories allow contributors to suggest labels like:

- bug
- enhancement
- documentation
- help wanted

Labels help categorize issues properly.

---

## Be Respectful and Professional

Even if you're frustrated, avoid aggressive language.

Bad:

```text
This is useless and broken. Fix it.
```

Better:

```text
I'm experiencing an issue with the login flow and would appreciate help resolving it.
```

Tone matters in open source communities.

---

## Example of a Good GitHub Issue

```text
Title: Login fails with 401 error after password reset

Description:
After resetting my password, I am unable to log in using the new credentials.

Expected:
User should be able to log in with updated password.

Actual:
Server returns 401 Unauthorized.

Steps to Reproduce:
1. Reset password
2. Go to login page
3. Enter new password
4. Click login
5. Receive 401 error

Environment:
OS: Windows 11
Browser: Chrome 120
Node: 20.x

Logs:
401 Unauthorized - Invalid credentials
```

---

## Common Mistakes

### Missing Reproduction Steps

Makes debugging difficult.

---

### No Environment Info

Issues become unclear.

---

### Too Vague Descriptions

“Doesn’t work” is not helpful.

---

### Combining Multiple Bugs

Creates confusion.

---

### Being Impatient or Rude

Slows down responses.

---

## A Simple GitHub Issue Template

```text
Title:

Description:

Expected Behavior:

Actual Behavior:

Steps to Reproduce:

Environment:

Logs/Screenshots:
```

Use this as a starting point.

---

## FAQ

### Why do maintainers ignore issues?

Usually because they are unclear, incomplete, or missing reproduction steps.

---

### Should I always include screenshots?

If the issue is visual or UI-related, yes.

---

### What if I don't know the exact cause?

That's okay. Just describe what you observed.

---

### Can beginners open GitHub issues?

Absolutely. Clear reporting is more important than experience.

---

### How long should an issue be?

Long enough to explain the problem clearly, not longer.

---

## Final Thoughts

A good GitHub issue is not about writing more—it’s about writing clearly.

When you provide structured, useful information:

```text
Clear Problem
↓
Easy Reproduction
↓
Faster Debugging
↓
Better Fix
```

You make life easier for maintainers and increase the chance your issue gets solved quickly.

Good communication is one of the most valuable skills in open source development.
